subject: Physics
question: The mass defect of a helium-4 nucleus is 0.0304 u. Calculate its binding energy in MeV and in joules, and its binding energy per nucleon. (1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻²; 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J)
response_text:
Binding energy: E = 0.0304 u × 931.5 MeV u⁻¹ = 28.3 MeV
Binding energy per nucleon: 28.3 MeV / 4 = 7.08 MeV ≈ 7.1 MeV
In joules, using 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J: E = 28.3 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 4.53 × 10⁻¹² J

Helium-4 has an unusually high binding energy per nucleon for a light nucleus, which is why alpha particles are so stable.
